solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Questionable if Pa's material for this role

definitions.text: Questionable if Pa's material for this role

indicators.note: something questionable is doubtful or dodgy, so the letters that follow are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: the possessive 's counts as a letter S here, giving PAS

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether Dad really has what it takes to be head of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Questionable' rearranges IF PAS MATERIAL; the whole clue also defines the answer, since Pa is just the man for the father-of-the-family role.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin title names the male head of a family, exactly the role a dad called Pa would fill.

clue.text: Permit response? Unusual for dogmatism

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the preceding words appear in an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: A permit is answered in a strangely dogmatic way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges the letters of PERMIT RESPONSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatism is a domineering insistence on one's views, which the noun for an overbearing, dictatorial manner describes.

clue.text: Write off entire amount

definitions.meaning: to wreck a car beyond repair, a sense of the verb in British slang
the full sum when everything is added up

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the slang verb for wrecking a vehicle and the noun for a complete sum.

clue.text: 'The Essence Of Scottish Diet' sold to real freak

indicators.note: a freak is something abnormal, so the letters of the preceding words come out in a freakish order

explanation.surface: A slogan about the heart of Scottish food is sold to a real oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freak' rearranges SOLD TO REAL. Porridge oats are the stereotypical core of the Scottish diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattened oats used for porridge are famously the staple of the traditional Scottish diet.

clue.text: You are said to support a fellow enthusiast

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the rest

parts.note: a mate is a fellow or companion

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are replaced by letters that sound like them

parts.note: the two words spoken aloud sound like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: Someone backs a friend who is a keen hobbyist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts the sound-alike UR beneath A MATE in this down entry; 'said' tells you to use letters that sound like 'you are'.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something out of enthusiasm rather than for pay, so a keen devotee fits.

clue.text: Not completely true batting partner once put on performance

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
an ex is a former partner
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A cricket memoir that is not quite accurate about a former batting partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' is a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is not precise, so it is only approximately rather than completely true.

clue.text: Capri for one is left- and right-hand drive

indicators.note: the right-hand end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone notes that on Capri cars may be driven from either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-hand' takes the last letter of 'drive'; the motoring surface hides the letter-picking.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island off Naples, an example of the poetic word for an island.

clue.text: Iota of mistrust

definitions.meaning: a tiny trace, as in a hint of garlic
a feeling of doubt about someone's honesty

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a slight trace of something and a feeling of distrust.

clue.text: Should one go commando under these?

definitions.text: Should one go commando under these?

parts.words: Should one go commando under these?
parts.note: going commando means wearing no underwear, and soldiers such as commandos wear a particular kind of rugged legwear

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about wearing nothing underneath military-style legwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat trousers are the loose, pocketed army trousers worn by soldiers, including commandos.

clue.text: About time The Greatest absorbed counter-attack

parts.note: re means about or concerning
boxer Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest
ate means took in or absorbed

explanation.surface: A boxing champion soaks up punishment before hitting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed' looks like a containment signal but simply gives ATE at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to strike back, which is what a counter-attack verb means.

clue.text: Rope made with twisted sisal — one disappearing with end of gaucho

indicators.note: twisted means turned out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
disappearing means the named piece is taken away from the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A South American cowboy's rope is made of twisted sisal fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disappearing' removes I (one) from SISAL, leaving SSAL; add O from 'end of gaucho' and 'twisted' rearranges SSALO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a looped rope used by cowboys such as gauchos to catch cattle.

clue.text: Same three notes restricting Lemmy's debut after Motorhead ruckus

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind this one

parts.note: read as motor's head, the first letter of motor is M

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the notes enclose the next piece

parts.note: E is a musical note, so three of the same note gives EEE

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: The rock band Motorhead and its frontman Lemmy play the same three notes in a noisy brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemmy fronted the heavy-metal band Motorhead. 'restricting' puts L (Lemmy's debut) inside EEE; 'after' places that behind M, the head of 'Motor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A melee is a confused, noisy scuffle, so a ruckus is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Lean cooking shows panache

indicators.note: cooking means fiddling or altering, as in cooking the books, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lean cooking is a stylish way to prepare food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is stylish flair and verve, a synonym of panache.

clue.text: Dare-devil may go out on one of these

definitions.text: Dare-devil may go out on one of these

parts.words: Dare-devil may go out on one of these
parts.note: the idiom of going out on something risky, literally a tree branch that may snap

explanation.surface: A risk-taker climbs out on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To go out on a limb is to take a risk; literally a limb is a tree branch.

clue.text: Hostile coup is unlikely without a gun being fired

indicators.note: without means outside, so the first group surrounds the second
unlikely suggests something improbable, signalling the letters come out in a strange order
being fired suggests going off in all directions, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: An improbable takeover is attempted without a shot being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' rearranges COUP IS to PCIOUS and 'being fired' rearranges A GUN to UGNA; 'without' wraps PCIOUS around UGNA, giving P-UGNA-CIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pugnacious person is eager to fight, which makes them hostile.

clue.text: Nan usually cooked in this tatty cap and back-to-front jumper

indicators.note: the cap of a word is its top or first letter
back-to-front means turned the wrong way round, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

explanation.surface: A grandmother in a scruffy hat and a jumper worn backwards does the cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nan' is the flatbread naan, not a grandmother; 'cap' takes T from 'tatty' and 'back-to-front' reverses ROO to OOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandoor is the clay oven in which Indian naan bread is traditionally baked.

clue.text: Narrow escape from ultimate heaven on earth in centre of Leamington Spa

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so the final letter is taken

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a phrase is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone narrowly avoids disaster in a place like heaven on earth, Leamington Spa.
explanation.walkthrough: Leamington Spa is an English spa town. 'centre of' picks G, the seventh of its thirteen letters; 'ultimate' takes N from 'heaven'.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a close call, an escape that very nearly failed.

clue.text: Spiv putting the squeeze on uninhibited Irish sightseer

indicators.note: squeezing something means pressing round it, so the first piece encloses the next

parts.note: a spiv is a flashy petty crook, like a tout selling tickets

indicators.note: read as un-in-hibited, the word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A shady dealer pressures a carefree Irish visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is a British term for a flashy black-market dealer. 'uninhibited' is read as un-in-hibited: the word sheds its outer letters, and 'putting the squeeze on' encloses what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone travelling to see the sights, so the meanings match.

clue.text: Sartre novel about ordinary hot day

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A novel by the French philosopher Sartre concerns an ordinary sweltering day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges SARTRE as RASTER and 'about' wraps it round O, giving R-O-ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaster is an informal word for a scorching hot day.

clue.text: Degenerate boy's consumed French roll

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up, so the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a roue is a debauched, degenerate man
a lad is a boy; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A dissolute boy gobbles a French bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French roll' is not a bread roll: the answer is a rolled dish with a French name. 'consumed' puts the boy inside the rake.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rolled-up slice of meat or sponge, its name French for something rolled.

clue.text: Dealer with six no trumps noting East's reluctant leads

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no trumps

indicators.note: the leads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A bridge dealer bids six no trumps while noticing that East leads reluctantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge surface makes 'Dealer' look like the card dealer; it is a wine merchant. 'leads' takes N, E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintner is a wine merchant, someone who deals in wine.

clue.text: With cape and island out of sight detective is at sea in small boat

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the remaining letters are jumbled
out of sight means gone, so the named letters are removed from the word

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: With the headland and island no longer visible, a detective is lost at sea in a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of sight' removes C and I from DETECTIVE, leaving DETETVE, which 'is at sea' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A vedette is a small fast naval patrol boat, originally a mounted sentry.

clue.text: Out to lunch (may contain these?)

definitions.meaning: slang for crazy or mentally absent
the allergy warning printed on food packaging, so a lunch might contain them

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for mad and also the allergen named in food warnings.

clue.text: Dog's beginning to drink dairy product

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dog starts lapping up something from the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes D from 'drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Curd is the thickened part of soured milk, a product of the dairy.

clue.text: Contrary characters caught in downpour — my concept of Wales

indicators.note: contrary means the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards
the letters held within the run of words form the piece

explanation.surface: Someone's idea of Wales is rain pouring down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards through 'downpoUR MY Concept' to find the letters, as 'characters caught in' and 'Contrary' signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymru is the Welsh-language name for Wales.

clue.text: Cockney professes his aspiration is one not looking too far ahead

definitions.text: one not looking too far ahead

indicators.note: a Cockney speaking drops the H sound at the start of words

parts.note: in his own words he would call his aspiration my hope

explanation.surface: A Londoner declares that his ambition is modest.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent drops initial H; aspiration also means the H sound, so the dropping is doubly signalled.
explanation.definitionFit: A myope is a short-sighted person, someone who cannot see far into the distance.

clue.text: Fruit picked up regularly throughout silly glut

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means lifted, so the letters are read upwards
taking letters at regular intervals through the phrase

explanation.surface: Fruit is gathered steadily from a silly surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly throughout' takes the even letters of SILLY GLUT, I L G U, and 'picked up' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross between a grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Police retiree in honey-trap

definitions.meaning: the singer who left the rock band the Police
a police trap using bait to catch criminals

explanation.definitionFit: Sting was the Police's lead singer, and a sting is a con or police entrapment operation.

clue.text: Miss start of vast party in Rome's all-weather venue

indicators.note: to miss the start is to leave out the first letter
in means placed inside, so the party goes into the city

parts.note: taken as the city name; the 's is a link
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A young woman starts a huge party in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman but is a verb meaning leave out. 'in' puts the party inside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astrodome in Houston was the first domed stadium, built so games could go on in any weather.

clue.text: Useless single challenged credulity

indicators.note: challenged means disputed or upset, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A useless lone voice challenged someone's gullibility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'challenged' rearranges USELESS SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilelessness is innocent lack of cunning, which leaves a person credulous and easily fooled.
